description: SONARIS es un equipo multidisciplinario enfocado en la ciencia, la tecnología y la innovación. Sus intereses abarcan la exploración espacial, la programación, el análisis de datos, la sonificación y el diseño digital. Integra perspectivas científicas, técnicas y creativas, con habilidades en investigación, desarrollo tecnológico, resolución de problemas y trabajo colaborativo.
summary: SONARIS is a Planetary Earth Information Jukebox that turns live Earth observation data into sound. NASA's Earth Information Center shows our changing planet through images alone, which leaves out everyone who cannot see them. SONARIS pairs live NASA satellite imagery with dynamic sonifications generated in real time: a pixel scan of NASA GIBS MODIS Terra imagery feeds a 4D atmospheric tensor into a Lorenz chaotic attractor, driving an FM synthesizer tuned to Earth's Schumann resonance (7.83 Hz) and consonant Lydian scales. Any city on Earth can be entered, and each place sings a different song  warmer places sound higher and brighter. Built as a zero-install web tool, SONARIS makes climate data accessible to blind and visually impaired people and turns Earth science into something anyone can hear and feel.
details: SONARIS is a web tool that lets anyone listen to Earth. The user types any city, country, or coordinates. The tool scans live NASA GIBS MODIS Terra satellite imagery pixel by pixel, extracts a 4D atmospheric tensor (red, green, blue, and vorticity from Navier-Stokes curl), and feeds it into a Lorenz strange attractor solved at 60 frames per second. The attractor's chaotic trajectory drives a Web Audio FM synthesizer tuned to Earth's Schumann resonance (7.83 Hz) and consonant Lydian scales, so the sound never repeats and always stays musical. Warmer, sunnier places produce higher, brighter sounds; colder, calmer places sound serene. The tool runs entirely in the browser with no installation and no pre-recorded files. We used NASA GIBS and the Earth Information Center, ESA Sentinel-5P for clouds and aerosols, JAXA GPM for precipitation, and Open-Meteo for real-time weather and geocoding. The project is creative because it translates sight into sound using chaos theory, making abstract climate data into a direct sensory experience. We designed it for accessibility first: blind and visually impaired people can perceive climate patterns through sound, and students can hear how the planet changes. The interface works for any place on Earth.
